mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates for future corporate earnings and increasing the present value of equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 7.0% over a 3-month window signals weakening labor market conditions, which may prompt the Federal Reserve to delay rate hikes or initiate easing, boosting equity valuations through lower real rates and improved risk appetite over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE exceeds 7.0% (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal fails to outperform baseline in 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in private demand, which increases the likelihood of a Fed rate cut, thereby supporting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 50% of instances, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98.0 for two consecutive months signals a contraction in real economic output, which increases the probability of a Fed rate cut and triggers a risk-on repositioning in equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO < 98.0 (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal generates negative returns in more than 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the growth rate of real personal consumption (measured via RSAFS) combined with a stable or declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates strong underlying demand momentum, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising RSAFS and stable UNRATE fails to generate positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the CPIAUCSL above 2.5% year-over-year, combined with a persistently low FEDFUNDS rate, signals inflationary pressures that may force the Fed to tighten policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS ≤ 1.0%, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200k per month, combined with a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tightening labor market that may lead to wage pressures and Fed rate hikes, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS > 200k and UNRATE < 7.5% (t-test p > 0.05), or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDP growth (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters, combined with weak industrial production (INDPRO), indicates a deepening economic slowdown that increases the likelihood of fiscal or monetary stimulus, boosting equity markets over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining GDPC1 and INDPRO fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term is not significant (p > 0.05).
